rationale: Noradrenaline resolved only via PubChem (InChIKey SFLSHLFXELFNJZ-QMMMGPOBSA-N, SMILES C1=CC(=C(C=C1[C@H](CN)O)O)O) with molecule_chembl_id = null under four synonyms (Noradrenaline, norepinephrine, levarterenol, L-noradrenaline), so chembl_known_activity at GPR85 (P60893) and chembl_ligand_promiscuity could not be run — the absence of a ChEMBL activity record here is a tool failure, not demonstrated novelty, and noradrenaline is in fact one of the most pharmacologically promiscuous endogenous metabolites known (the nine adrenergic receptors ADRA1A/B/D, ADRA2A/B/C, ADRB1/2/3, plus transporters SLC6A2/SLC6A3/SLC6A4 and metabolising enzymes). GPR85 (SREB2) is annotated in UniProt simply as "Orphan receptor", a 7TM GPCR at the cell membrane, so there is no orthosteric-site expectation to confirm or contradict, and a high AF3 ipTM (0.93) with ligand pLDDT 79.9 is the expected result for a small catecholamine dropped into a GPCR bundle rather than evidence of a specific interaction. The supplied screen data (2 of 11 receptors confident; CCD-code fold 0.93/0.92 vs SMILES fold 0.90/0.92 straddling the 0.91 gate) is not stable enough to carry the claim on its own.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: UniProt P60893 lists keyword Glycoprotein with 3 Glycosylation sites and 1 Disulfide bond. pubmed_ptm_glycosylation for GPR85 returned a single hit (PMID 42563402, SREB orphan receptor roles in fish ovary), which is not about PTMs at all. Glycosylation on the extracellular face is a general caveat for any AF3 bare-sequence model of this receptor, but it concerns the protein side only and is not the basis of this verdict; without a fold I could not check whether any of the 3 sites lands on the modeled pocket.

Because no ChEMBL id was obtained, chembl_known_activity at GPR85/P60893 and chembl_ligand_promiscuity returned no number — promiscuity is therefore argued from the known pharmacology (adrenergic alpha1A/B/D, alpha2A/B/C, beta1/2/3 receptors and the monoamine transporters), i.e. many distinct measured targets, not from a retrieved count. AF3 metrics supplied: ipTM 0.93, ligand pLDDT 79.9, BSA 465 A^2; no ligands block (buried_fraction, pocket topology, clash) was available since fold_complex is disabled in this run.
follow_up: (1) Re-resolve noradrenaline against ChEMBL directly (it is CHEMBL1437/"NOREPINEPHRINE" in most builds) and run chembl_ligand_promiscuity plus chembl_known_activity against P60893 — the promiscuity count is the single number that would firm this verdict up. (2) The fold I would have run but could not in this run: GPR85 + this SMILES with the ligands block read out, to check buried_fraction (>=0.7 for a real pocket), pocket topology (contacts must fall on Transmembrane segments, with ECL residues — a cytoplasmic or ECL-only pose is a negative result about the pose), clash and min_separation_A. (3) The decisive experiment is the counter-screen: fold noradrenaline against 2-3 unrelated non-aminergic receptors; if they score comparably to 0.93, the confidence is not specific to GPR85. (4) Wet-lab: a cAMP/beta-arrestin or GTP-gamma-S assay on GPR85-transfected cells with a noradrenaline dose-response, with an adrenergic-receptor-null background to exclude endogenous alpha/beta receptor signal.

rationale: GPR153 (UniProt Q6NV75) is annotated simply as "Orphan receptor", a 7-TM class-A-like GPCR at the cell membrane, so a catecholamine-sized pocket is chemically plausible and the ipTM=0.92 / ligand pLDDT 79.4 fold is exactly the expected result for a small molecule placed in a GPCR bundle, not evidence of specificity (median interface pTM for metabolite candidates in this screen was 0.85). The supplied screen data themselves show the result is representation-dependent: CCD LNR gave interface pTM 0.93/0.92 but the same molecule from SMILES gave 0.90/0.92, straddling the 0.91 gate, so the "confident" call is not robust; the molecule was nonetheless confident at only 2 of 11 receptors tested, which is the one mildly favourable discriminating fact here. Noradrenaline is the canonical endogenous agonist of the nine adrenergic receptors and is additionally active at TAAR1, monoamine transporters and metabolising enzymes, i.e. a highly promiscuous endogenous catecholamine, so a further confident pose adds little.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: UniProt ptm_topology_feature_counts for GPR153 lists only Topological domain (8) and Transmembrane (7) — no annotated Glycosylation or Lipidation sites, and no PTM-category keywords. pubmed_ptm_glycosylation returned a single hit (PMID 40623996, Nat Commun 2025, GPR153 in vascular damage responses via cAMP/YAP-TAZ/NF-kB), which is a signalling paper and not about glycosylation. No PTM artifact concern on the receptor side.

rationale: The two checks that discriminate for a small-molecule partner could not be completed: chembl_known_activity (Q8NGU9 vs CHEMBL96) and chembl_ligand_promiscuity (CHEMBL96) each returned a ChEMBL server 500 error on two attempts, so neither novelty at GPR150 nor the molecule's target breadth was measured in this run. The remaining evidence is favourable but not sufficient on its own: GPR150 is a UniProt-annotated orphan GPCR (Q8NGU9, "Orphan receptor", 7 transmembrane segments) with HPA RNA in brain (2.5 nTPM) and pancreas (6.5 nTPM), the same two tissues where the producer GAD2 is expressed (brain 65.4 nTPM; pancreatic islet cells 563.0 nCPM), and the supplied breadth screen shows GABA passing the calibrated gate at only 2 of 19 receptors tested. The AF3 ipTM of 0.91 is the expected result for a small molecule in a pocket and is not counted as evidence of specific binding.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: UniProt lists no Glycosylation or Lipidation features for GPR150 (feature counts are only Topological domain 8 and Transmembrane 7) and no PTM-category keywords. pubmed_ptm_glycosylation returned 1 hit, PMID 6178845 on visna virus precursor polypeptides (1982), which is unrelated to this receptor. There is no evidence for a receptor-side PTM artifact, though absence of annotation on an understudied orphan receptor is weak evidence.
known_interaction_evidence: No measured-affinity record could be retrieved because chembl_known_activity errored twice (ChEMBL 500). UniProt describes GPR150 only as "Orphan receptor", with no endogenous ligand of any chemical class annotated, so there is no documented competing ligand class for the pocket, and equally no documented support for GABA. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence were not queried because they index protein pairs and do not index a metabolite against a receptor.
